$comment: Catalog of third-party scanners `vulnetix gha setup <tool>` can wire into a
repository, and the single source of truth for the published examples.
Every entry is transcribed from a workflow that actually runs in production,
not from a tool's README. The shell steps carry the exit-code handling and
SARIF validation those tools genuinely need: `tool > out.sarif` leaves a
zero-byte file when the tool fails, `if-no-files-found` cannot detect that
because the file exists, and the result gets published as a scan report.
Pinning: third-party actions and container images are pinned so a scan is
reproducible and cannot change output shape without a change here. The
Vulnetix CLI itself is deliberately NOT pinned — install.sh resolves the
latest release, so a workflow written today keeps working without edits.
`category` must be one of the Vulnetix scan categories, and decides which
/v2/cli.<category>-sarif endpoint the report is filed under. It is advisory
here: the CLI infers the category from the report itself and the server
fixes it from the route, so a wrong value here cannot misfile a finding.

tools.name: gosec
tools.description: Go static analysis for common security mistakes.

tools.name: OSV-Scanner
tools.description: Dependency vulnerabilities from the OSV database.

tools.name: Semgrep
tools.description: Multi-language static analysis with community rulesets.

steps.name: Run Semgrep
steps.run:
python3 -m pip install --quiet --break-system-packages semgrep
semgrep scan --config auto --sarif --output semgrep.sarif .

tools.name: Grype
tools.description: Vulnerability matching against the installed dependency set.

tools.name: Trivy (filesystem)
tools.description: Dependency scan of the checked-out tree, as both CycloneDX and SARIF.
tools.note: Trivy reports the driver name "Trivy" for every scan mode, so the artifact name is the only thing that distinguishes a filesystem scan from a config scan. Keep it.

tools.name: Trivy (config)
tools.description: Misconfiguration scan of IaC and Dockerfiles.
tools.note: The artifact name must stay "trivy-config" so this is not filed as an SCA scan; see the trivy-fs note.

tools.name: Checkov
tools.description: Policy-as-code checks for Terraform, CloudFormation, Kubernetes and more.
tools.note: Checkov writes its SARIF as results.sarif, the same filename KICS uses. Tool identity comes from the SARIF driver and the artifact name, never the filename.

steps.name: Run Checkov
steps.run:
python3 -m pip install --quiet --break-system-packages checkov
checkov -d . -o sarif --output-file-path . --soft-fail || true

steps.name: Run KICS
steps.run:
mkdir -p kics-out
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/path" checkmarx/kics:v2.1.20 \
  scan -p /path -o /path/kics-out --report-formats sarif --no-progress || true

steps.name: Run Terrascan
steps.run:
set -uo pipefail
# terrascan writes SARIF to stdout and logs to stderr, so the redirect must
# separate them. Exit 3 means violations were found and 5 means no IaC was
# present; neither is a failure of the scan itself.
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/iac" tenable/terrascan:1.19.9 \
  scan -i terraform -d /iac -o sarif >terrascan.sarif 2>terrascan.stderr
rc=$?
case "$rc" in
  0|3) ;;
  5)   echo "::notice::terrascan found no IaC files" ;;
  *)   echo "::warning::terrascan exited $rc"; sed -n '1,20p' terrascan.stderr ;;
esac
# Without this guard a failed run leaves a zero-byte or half-written file that
# `if-no-files-found` cannot detect, and it gets published as a "SARIF report".
if ! jq -e '.version and (.runs | type == "array")' terrascan.sarif >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "::warning::terrascan produced no valid SARIF; dropping the artifact"
  rm -f terrascan.sarif
fi

tools.name: tfsec
tools.description: Terraform static analysis. Upstream now recommends Trivy config.

tools.name: zizmor
tools.description: Finds security problems in the workflows themselves.

steps.name: Run zizmor
steps.run:
set -uo pipefail
python3 -m pip install --quiet --break-system-packages zizmor
# zizmor exits 14 when it has findings, which is a successful scan.
zizmor --format sarif . >zizmor.sarif 2>zizmor.stderr
rc=$?
if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && [ "$rc" -ne 14 ]; then
  echo "::warning::zizmor exited $rc"; sed -n '1,20p' zizmor.stderr
fi
if ! jq -e '.version and (.runs | type == "array")' zizmor.sarif >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "::warning::zizmor produced no valid SARIF; dropping the artifact"
  rm -f zizmor.sarif
fi

steps.name: Run Clippy
steps.run:
set -uo pipefail
rustup component add clippy
cargo install clippy-sarif sarif-fmt
# cargo clippy exits non-zero when it emits warnings, which is a successful run.
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --message-format=json \
  | clippy-sarif >clippy.sarif 2>clippy.stderr
if ! jq -e '.version and (.runs | type == "array")' clippy.sarif >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "::warning::clippy produced no valid SARIF; dropping the artifact"
  sed -n '1,20p' clippy.stderr
  rm -f clippy.sarif
fi

tools.name: Gitleaks
tools.description: Hardcoded secret detection across the working tree and history.

steps.name: Run Gitleaks
steps.run:
set -uo pipefail
# Gitleaks exits 1 when it finds leaks, which is a successful scan.
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/repo" zricethezav/gitleaks:v8.24.0 \
  detect --source /repo --report-format sarif --report-path /repo/gitleaks.sarif --no-git || true
if ! jq -e '.version and (.runs | type == "array")' gitleaks.sarif >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "::warning::gitleaks produced no valid SARIF; dropping the artifact"
  rm -f gitleaks.sarif
fi
